<skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

display.text:
"""Error types for Agentic ODI operations.

Every failure mode in the domain has a dedicated exception class so callers
can branch on the *kind* of failure instead of matching on message text. All
ODI errors inherit from :class:`OdiError`, so a single ``except OdiError``
catches anything this package raises deliberately.

Note that :class:`ValidationError` here is the *ODI contract* error. Pydantic's
own ``ValidationError`` remains available from ``pydantic`` and is unrelated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


class OdiError(Exception):
    """Base class for every deliberate Agentic ODI failure."""


class ValidationError(OdiError, ValueError):
    """Input did not satisfy the ODI contract.

    Also a :class:`ValueError` so that callers written against the previous
    behaviour (which raised bare ``ValueError``) keep working unchanged.
    """


class NotFoundError(OdiError):
    """A referenced resource does not exist.

    ``hint`` is an optional sentence telling the caller what to do next. It is
    appended to the message so it survives into user-facing output.
    """

    def __init__(self, resource_id: str, kind: str, hint: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.resource_id = resource_id
        self.kind = kind
        self.hint = hint or ""
        message = f"{kind} not found: {resource_id}"
        if self.hint:
            message = f"{message}. {self.hint}"
        super().__init__(message)


class ConflictError(OdiError):
    """The requested change conflicts with the current state."""


class RateLimitError(OdiError):
    """The caller exceeded an allowed rate or volume."""

    def __init__(
        self, message: str = "Rate limit exceeded", retry_after: float | None = None
    ) -> None:
        self.retry_after = retry_after
        super().__init__(message)


class ConsentRequired(OdiError):
    """The agent tried to act on the workspace before the PM agreed to it."""


class StoreError(OdiError):
    """The persistence layer could not complete the operation."""


class SerializationError(OdiError):
    """A payload could not be converted to or from its wire format."""


_STATUS_BY_ERROR: tuple[tuple[type[OdiError], int], ...] = (
    (ValidationError, 400),
    (NotFoundError, 404),
    (ConflictError, 409),
    (RateLimitError, 429),
    (ConsentRequired, 403),
    (StoreError, 500),
    (SerializationError, 502),
)


def error_status(err: OdiError) -> int:
    """Map an ODI error onto the HTTP status code that best describes it.

    Unknown :class:`OdiError` subclasses fall back to ``500`` rather than
    raising, so a new error type can never break an error handler.
    """
    for error_type, status in _STATUS_BY_ERROR:
        if isinstance(err, error_type):
            return status
    return 500

# Data Flow

## Sources of Truth

| Layer | Owns | Persists |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
| `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | `build_repository()` selects SQLite in production and in-memory for `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` |
| `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop, conversation history, PM memory | Via the same repository when the local backend is active; conversations and memory in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
| `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
| `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |

## Write Paths

### Local CLI

```text
agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
  -> LocalBackend
  -> ODIService
  -> SQLiteRepository
  -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
```

### MCP

```text
MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
  -> FastMCP tool
  -> ODIService
  -> configured Repository
```

`apps/mcp-server` builds its repository once at import time with `build_repository()`. Production uses SQLite; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` (the root test suite does this in `tests/conftest.py`).

### Studio API

```text
apps/studio SPA
  -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
  -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
  -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository

apps/studio SPA
  -> /api/chat
  -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
  -> StudioMemory (conversation turns + remembered observations)
```

The studio memory is a separate SQLite file, not an ODI repository. It never
feeds the canvas; it only supplies bounded context to the next chat turn.

The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.

## Read Paths

```text
ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
  -> Repository read-through state
  -> Pydantic models
  -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
```

The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.

## Configuration

| Variable | Used by | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB` | Studio API memory | `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/studio/dist` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |

## Trust Boundaries

- The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
- The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
- MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.

## The Failure Path

A failure is a first-class result, not an empty success. The path is the same
for the CLI, the sidecar, and the SPA.

```text
MCP tool result (text)
  -> agentic_odi_core.remote.parse_tool_result
  -> StudioError { code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id }
  -> sidecar: StudioHTTPError -> HTTP status + {"error": StudioError}
  -> SPA: StudioApiError -> FailurePanel (message, detail, suggestion, Retry)
```

- **One error body.** Every HTTP failure is `{"error": StudioError}`. The SPA
  also reads a legacy `{"detail": "..."}` body, so an older sidecar still
  produces a readable message. Write routes no longer wrap their result in
  `{"ok": true, "result": ...}`: a success is the object, a delete is
  `{"deleted": id}`.
- **One terminal chat event.** Every `/api/chat` stream ends with exactly one
  `message` or one `error`. A recoverable tool error stays a tool result the
  model can read, but it is reported as `status: "error"` and counted. A fatal
  failure ends the stream with `event: error` carrying the `StudioError`.
- **Request ids.** The sidecar accepts or mints `X-Request-ID`, echoes it on
  the response, and puts it on every SSE frame. The MCP server's own log line
  and the `Execution` record (#82) do not carry it yet, and authentication
  (#90) is out of scope.
- **The canvas is a union.** `CanvasState` is `loading | ready | empty |
  error`. An empty canvas is an invitation; a failed canvas is a failure panel
  with Retry. The two never look the same.
- **The turn log is safe.** One JSON line per turn carries the request id, the
  model, the round and tool counts, the error count, the duration, and the
  outcome. Sensitive keys are dropped rather than redacted, so no token, key,
  or customer quote can reach the log.

1: """HTTP error shape, status mapping, and request-id handling for the sidecar.
2: 
3: Every failure the Studio API reports travels as one body::
4: 
5:     {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "detail": ..., "suggestion": ...,
6:                "retryable": ..., "request_id": ...}}
7: 
8: The model itself lives in :mod:`agentic_odi_core.remote` so the CLI and the
9: sidecar agree on what a failure is; this module owns the HTTP mapping.
10: """
11: 
12: from __future__ import annotations
13: 
14: import logging
15: import re
16: from typing import Any
17: from uuid import uuid4
18: 
19: from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
20: from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
21: from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
22: from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
23: from starlette.datastructures import Headers, MutableHeaders
24: from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
25: from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
26: 
27: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
28: 
29: REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID"
30: 
31: #: A request id is echoed in responses and written to logs, so it must be a
32: #: short, boring token. Anything else is replaced with a fresh one.
33: REQUEST_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$")
34: 
35: STATUS_FOR_CODE: dict[StudioErrorCode, int] = {
36:     StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND: 404,
37:     StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION: 422,
38:     StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE: 422,
39:     StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT: 409,
40:     StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE: 502,
41:     StudioErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 502,
42:     StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED: 500,
43:     StudioErrorCode.LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED: 500,
44:     StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL: 500,
45: }
46: 
47: CODE_FOR_STATUS: dict[int, StudioErrorCode] = {
48:     400: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
49:     404: StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
50:     409: StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT,
51:     422: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
52:     500: StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
53:     502: StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
54: }

56: 
57: class StudioHTTPError(Exception):
58:     """A failure that already knows its HTTP status and its error model."""
59: 
60:     def __init__(self, error: StudioError, status_code: int | None = None) -> None:
61:         self.error = error
62:         self.status_code = status_code if status_code is not None else status_for_code(error.code)
63:         super().__init__(error.message)
64: 
65: 
66: def status_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode) -> int:
67:     """Return the HTTP status that belongs to an error code."""
68:     return STATUS_FOR_CODE.get(code, 500)
69: 
70: 
71: def code_for_status(status_code: int) -> StudioErrorCode:

76: def request_id_for(request: Request) -> str:
77:     """Return the request id assigned to this request, or an empty string."""
78:     return str(getattr(request.state, "request_id", "") or "")
79: 
80: 
81: def _error_body(request: Request, error: StudioError) -> dict[str, Any]:
82:     request_id = request_id_for(request)

88: def _error_response(request: Request, error: StudioError, status_code: int) -> JSONResponse:
89:     request_id = request_id_for(request)
90:     headers = {REQUEST_ID_HEADER: request_id} if request_id else None
91:     return JSONResponse(_error_body(request, error), status_code=status_code, headers=headers)

94: def studio_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StudioHTTPError) -> JSONResponse:

99: def validation_error_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
100:     """Render a request-body validation failure as a ``validation`` error."""
101:     detail = _compact_validation_text(exc)
102:     error = StudioError(
103:         code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,

111: def _compact_validation_text(exc: RequestValidationError) -> str:

"""HTTP error shape, status mapping, and request-id handling for the sidecar.

Every failure the Studio API reports travels as one body::

    {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "detail": ..., "suggestion": ...,
               "retryable": ..., "request_id": ...}}

The model itself lives in :mod:`agentic_odi_core.remote` so the CLI and the
sidecar agree on what a failure is; this module owns the HTTP mapping.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4

from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.datastructures import Headers, MutableHeaders
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID"

#: A request id is echoed in responses and written to logs, so it must be a
#: short, boring token. Anything else is replaced with a fresh one.
REQUEST_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$")

STATUS_FOR_CODE: dict[StudioErrorCode, int] = {
    StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND: 404,
    StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION: 422,
    StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE: 422,
    StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT: 409,
    StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE: 502,
    StudioErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 502,
    StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED: 500,
    StudioErrorCode.LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED: 500,
    StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL: 500,
}

CODE_FOR_STATUS: dict[int, StudioErrorCode] = {
    400: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
    404: StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
    409: StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT,
    422: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
    500: StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
    502: StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
}


class StudioHTTPError(Exception):
    """A failure that already knows its HTTP status and its error model."""

    def __init__(self, error: StudioError, status_code: int | None = None) -> None:
        self.error = error
        self.status_code = status_code if status_code is not None else status_for_code(error.code)
        super().__init__(error.message)


def status_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode) -> int:
    """Return the HTTP status that belongs to an error code."""
    return STATUS_FOR_CODE.get(code, 500)


def code_for_status(status_code: int) -> StudioErrorCode:
    """Return the error code that belongs to an HTTP status."""
    return CODE_FOR_STATUS.get(status_code, StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL)


def request_id_for(request: Request) -> str:
    """Return the request id assigned to this request, or an empty string."""
    return str(getattr(request.state, "request_id", "") or "")


def _error_body(request: Request, error: StudioError) -> dict[str, Any]:
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    if not error.request_id:
        error = error.model_copy(update={"request_id": request_id})
    return {"error": error.model_dump(mode="json")}


def _error_response(request: Request, error: StudioError, status_code: int) -> JSONResponse:
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    headers = {REQUEST_ID_HEADER: request_id} if request_id else None
    return JSONResponse(_error_body(request, error), status_code=status_code, headers=headers)


def studio_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StudioHTTPError) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a :class:`StudioHTTPError` as the one error body."""
    return _error_response(request, exc.error, exc.status_code)


def validation_error_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a request-body validation failure as a ``validation`` error."""
    detail = _compact_validation_text(exc)
    error = StudioError(
        code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
        message="Request validation failed.",
        detail=detail,
        suggestion="Check the request body and try again.",
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, 422)


def _compact_validation_text(exc: RequestValidationError) -> str:
    parts: list[str] = []
    for error in exc.errors():
        location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
        parts.append(f"{location}: {error.get('msg', 'invalid')}")
    return "; ".join(parts)


def http_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a Starlette/FastAPI ``HTTPException`` as the one error body."""
    error = StudioError(
        code=code_for_status(exc.status_code),
        message=str(exc.detail),
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, exc.status_code)


def unhandled_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    """Log an unexpected failure and return it without internals."""
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    logger.exception("unhandled studio-api error (request_id=%s)", request_id, exc_info=exc)
    error = StudioError(
        code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
        message="Something went wrong. The team has been notified.",
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, 500)


def _safe_request_id(candidate: str | None) -> str:
    """Return the client's request id when it is safe to echo, else a fresh one."""
    if candidate and REQUEST_ID_PATTERN.match(candidate):
        return candidate
    return uuid4().hex


class RequestIdMiddleware:
    """Accept or mint an ``X-Request-ID`` and echo it on the response."""

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        request_id = _safe_request_id(Headers(scope=scope).get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER))
        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id

        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                MutableHeaders(scope=message)[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = request_id
            await send(message)

        await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)


def register_error_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Install the one-error-body handlers on an app."""
    handler: Any = studio_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(StudioHTTPError, handler)
    handler = validation_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, handler)
    handler = http_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, handler)
    handler = unhandled_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, handler)

613: async def stream_chat(

622:     ``error``. A failure is never dressed up as a success, and it never leaves

627:     counters = {"rounds": 0, "tool_calls": 0, "tool_errors": 0, "rounds_exhausted": 0}

658:             tool_calls=counters["tool_calls"],
659:             tool_errors=counters["tool_errors"],
660:             duration_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),

"""Conversational helper with offline fallbacks and a streaming tool loop.

The loop fans the MCP tools and three local tools — ``render_ui``,
``remember``, and ``add_connector`` — into the completion. Local tools are
intercepted rather than forwarded: ``render_ui`` validates its spec against the
catalog the client sent and streams a ``ui`` event, ``remember`` stores a
suggested observation and streams a ``memory`` event, and ``add_connector``
writes the shared connector registry and streams a ``connector`` event.

The conversation is persisted when a memory store is supplied, so a PM can leave
and come back to the same thread and the same working context.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import time
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

1: /**
2:  * The first-run context conversation, as data.
3:  *
4:  * Four questions, one at a time, each skippable. Keeping the script pure makes
5:  * the pacing and the copy testable without rendering anything.
6:  */
7: 
8: import type { StudioBrief } from "../types";
9: 
10: export type BriefField = "product_name" | "target_user" | "job_statement" | "core_problem";
11: 
12: export type SetupDraft = Record<BriefField, string>;
13: 
14: export interface SetupQuestion {
15:   field: BriefField;
16:   /** Short label used by the review and the change chips. */
17:   label: string;
18:   ask: string;
19:   hint: string;
20:   placeholder: string;
21:   quickReplies?: string[];
22: }
23: 
24: export const SETUP_QUESTIONS: SetupQuestion[] = [
25:   {
26:     field: "product_name",
27:     label: "Product",
28:     ask: "What are you building?",
29:     hint: "A product, a service, a team — whatever the work is.",
30:     placeholder: "Ambient — a deployment tool",
31:   },
32:   {
33:     field: "target_user",
34:     label: "Customer",
35:     ask: "Who feels the problem most?",
36:     hint: "The people whose job you are trying to make easier.",
37:     placeholder: "Platform engineers shipping services",
38:   },
39:   {
40:     field: "job_statement",
41:     label: "Job",
42:     ask: "What job are they trying to get done?",
43:     hint: "The progress they want, not a feature.",
44:     placeholder: "Get a service from commit to production without hand-copying config",
45:   },
46:   {
47:     field: "core_problem",
48:     label: "Friction",
49:     ask: "Where does it hurt most?",
50:     hint: "One frustration is enough.",
51:     placeholder: "A missed config key costs hours on deploy day",
52:     quickReplies: [
53:       "It takes too long",
54:       "It is error-prone",
55:       "It is too manual",
56:       "It is hard to find what I need",
57:     ],
58:   },
59: ];
60: 
61: export const QUESTION_COUNT = SETUP_QUESTIONS.length;
62: 
63: /** The phase index meaning "show the review instead of a question". */
64: export const REVIEW_INDEX = QUESTION_COUNT;
65: 
66: export function emptyDraft(): SetupDraft {
67:   return {
68:     product_name: "",
69:     target_user: "",
70:     job_statement: "",
71:     core_problem: "",
72:   };
73: }
74: 
75: export function draftFromBrief(brief: Partial<StudioBrief> | null): SetupDraft {
76:   return {
77:     product_name: brief?.product_name ?? "",
78:     target_user: brief?.target_user ?? "",
79:     job_statement: brief?.job_statement ?? "",
80:     core_problem: brief?.core_problem ?? "",
81:   };
82: }
83: 
84: export function draftHasContent(draft: SetupDraft): boolean {
85:   return SETUP_QUESTIONS.some((question) => draft[question.field].trim().length > 0);
86: }
87: 
88: /** Where a resumed conversation should pick up: the first unanswered question. */
89: export function firstUnanswered(draft: SetupDraft): number {
90:   const index = SETUP_QUESTIONS.findIndex(
91:     (question) => draft[question.field].trim().length === 0,
92:   );
93:   return index === -1 ? REVIEW_INDEX : index;
94: }
95: 
96: const REFLECTIONS: Record<BriefField, (value: string) => string> = {
97:   product_name: (value) => `Got it — ${value}.`,
98:   target_user: (value) => `So it is for ${value}.`,
99:   job_statement: (value) => `That is the job: ${value}.`,
100:   core_problem: () => "Then that is where we start.",
101: };
102: 
103: export function reflectionFor(field: BriefField, value: string): string {
104:   return REFLECTIONS[field](value);
105: }
106: 
107: export function questionContent(
108:   index: number,
109:   draft: SetupDraft,
110:   lead?: string,
111: ): string {
112:   const question = SETUP_QUESTIONS[index];
113:   if (!question) {
114:     return reviewContent(draft);
115:   }
116:   const current = draft[question.field].trim();
117:   return [lead, `**${question.ask}**`, `_${question.hint}_`, current ? `You said: “${current}”.` : ""]
118:     .filter(Boolean)
119:     .join("\n\n");
120: }
121: 
122: export function reviewContent(draft: SetupDraft): string {
123:   if (!draftHasContent(draft)) {
124:     return "Nothing yet — that is completely fine. We can start exploring and I will ask when it matters.";
125:   }
126:   const lines = SETUP_QUESTIONS.map((question) => {
127:     const value = draft[question.field].trim();
128:     return `- **${question.label}** — ${value || "—"}`;
129:   });
130:   return ["Here is what I will hold:", "", ...lines].join("\n");
131: }
132: 
133: const SAVE_PHRASE = /\b(looks? right|save|done|good|yes|ok|okay|ship it|let'?s go|go ahead)\b/i;
134: 
135: export function isSavePhrase(text: string): boolean {
136:   return SAVE_PHRASE.test(text.trim());
137: }
138: 
139: const FIELD_HINTS: Array<{ field: BriefField; pattern: RegExp }> = [
140:   { field: "target_user", pattern: /\b(customer|audience|user|who it|who is|who feels)\b/i },
141:   { field: "job_statement", pattern: /\b(job|trying to do|progress|outcome)\b/i },
142:   { field: "core_problem", pattern: /\b(friction|pain|problem|hurt|stuck|frustrat)\b/i },
143:   { field: "product_name", pattern: /\b(product|building|service|tool|what it is)\b/i },
144: ];
145: 
146: /** Recognise "change the job" style replies in the review. */
147: export function fieldFromText(text: string): BriefField | null {
148:   return FIELD_HINTS.find((entry) => entry.pattern.test(text))?.field ?? null;
149: }
150: 
151: export function isQuestionFilled(draft: SetupDraft, index: number): boolean {
152:   const question = SETUP_QUESTIONS[index];
153:   return Boolean(question && draft[question.field].trim());
154: }
155: 
156: export type SetupIntent =
157:   | { kind: "skip" }
158:   | { kind: "explore" }
159:   /** A step that belongs in the conversation, not in a view. */
160:   | { kind: "talk"; text: string }
161:   | {
162:       kind: "panel";
163:       panel: "landscape" | "jobmap" | "evidence" | "capture" | "settings";
164:     };
165: 
166: const SKIP_PHRASE = /\b(skip|pass|not sure|no idea|don'?t know|unsure)\b/i;
167: const EXPLORE_PHRASE = /^(explore|later|not now|maybe later|let me look around)\b/i;
168: const OPEN_PHRASE = /^(show|open|go to|take me to|view)\b/i;
169: 
170: /**
171:  * Read a free-text reply as an intent before treating it as an answer.
172:  * This is what keeps the conversation from swallowing "skip" or "show me the
173:  * landscape" as a product name.
174:  */
175: export function parseSetupIntent(text: string): SetupIntent | null {
176:   const value = text.trim();
177:   if (!value) {
178:     return null;
179:   }
180:   if (SKIP_PHRASE.test(value)) {
181:     return { kind: "skip" };
182:   }
183:   if (EXPLORE_PHRASE.test(value)) {
184:     return { kind: "explore" };
185:   }
186:   const opening = OPEN_PHRASE.test(value);
187:   const lower = value.toLowerCase();
188:   if (opening || lower === "landscape") {
189:     if (/landscape|opportunit/.test(lower)) {
190:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "landscape" };
191:     }
192:     if (/job map|steps?/.test(lower)) {
193:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "jobmap" };
194:     }
195:     if (/impact|simulat/.test(lower)) {
196:       return {
197:         kind: "talk",
198:         text:
199:           "Simulate the impact of a bet on my most underserved opportunity. " +
200:           "Ask me what the bet is, then show me what changes before and after.",
201:       };
202:     }
203:     if (/evidence/.test(lower)) {
204:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "evidence" };
205:     }
206:     if (/capture|add an outcome/.test(lower)) {
207:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "capture" };
208:     }
209:     if (/settings?/.test(lower)) {
210:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "settings" };
211:     }
212:   }
213:   return null;
214: }

1: /**
2:  * Free-plan Living Studio Worker.
3:  *
4:  * Workers Static Assets serve the built SPA from `apps/studio/dist`. Requests under
5:  * `/api/*` are forwarded to the Python sidecar (`apps/studio-api`), which runs on
6:  * the developer's machine and is published by a free Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.
7:  * (Running the sidecar inside Cloudflare requires Workers Containers, which is
8:  * a paid-plan feature.)
9:  */
10: 
11: interface Env {
12:   ASSETS: Fetcher;
13:   /** Public origin of the sidecar, e.g. https://random.trycloudflare.com */
14:   SIDECAR_URL?: string;
15: }
16: 
17: const API_PREFIX = "/api/";
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Defense-in-depth headers on every Response, assets and API alike.
21:  *
22:  * The SPA loads only its own bundle, talks to the Worker origin at `/api/*`, and
23:  * uses React inline styles, hence `'unsafe-inline'` for styles but nothing for
24:  * scripts. `connect-src 'self'` keeps a compromised bundle from exfiltrating
25:  * to another origin; `frame-ancestors` repeats the `X-Frame-Options` intent for
26:  * browsers that only honor the CSP directive.
27:  */
28: const SECURITY_HEADERS: Record<string, string> = {
29:   "Content-Security-Policy": [
30:     "default-src 'self'",
31:     "script-src 'self'",
32:     "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
33:     "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
34:     "font-src 'self' data:",
35:     "connect-src 'self'",
36:     "object-src 'none'",
37:     "base-uri 'self'",
38:     "form-action 'self'",
39:     "frame-ancestors 'none'",
40:   ].join("; "),
41:   "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
42:   "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
43:   "Referrer-Policy": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin",
44:   "Permissions-Policy": "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()",
45: };
46: 
47: function secure(response: Response): Response {
48:   const headers = new Headers(response.headers);
49:   for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(SECURITY_HEADERS)) {
50:     headers.set(name, value);
51:   }
52:   // Reuse the body stream so SSE (`/api/chat`) keeps streaming.
53:   return new Response(response.body, {
54:     status: response.status,
55:     statusText: response.statusText,
56:     headers,
57:   });
58: }
59: 
60: function sidecarError(detail: string): Response {
61:   return Response.json({ detail }, { status: 502 });
62: }
63: 
64: export default {
65:   async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
66:     const url = new URL(request.url);
67: 
68:     if (!url.pathname.startsWith(API_PREFIX)) {
69:       return secure(await env.ASSETS.fetch(request));
70:     }
71: 
72:     const sidecar = env.SIDECAR_URL?.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "");
73:     if (!sidecar) {
74:       return secure(sidecarError("SIDECAR_URL is not configured"));
75:     }
76: 
77:     // The Quick Tunnel routes by hostname, so the Worker's Host must not leak.
78:     const headers = new Headers(request.headers);
79:     headers.delete("host");
80:     headers.delete("cf-connecting-ip");
81: 
82:     const target = new URL(`${url.pathname}${url.search}`, `${sidecar}/`);
83: 
84:     try {
85:       // Returning the upstream Response directly preserves SSE streaming for
86:       // `/api/chat`.
87:       return secure(
88:         await fetch(
89:           new Request(target, {
90:             method: request.method,
91:             headers,
92:             body: request.body,
93:             redirect: "manual",
94:           }),
95:         ),
96:       );
97:     } catch (error) {
98:       return secure(sidecarError(`Sidecar unreachable: ${(error as Error).message}`));
99:     }
100:   },
101: } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

app = typer.Typer(

    help="Alias for customer-outcomes.",
    hidden=True,
)

def _version_callback(ctx: typer.Context, value: bool) -> None:
    if value:
        if ctx.params.get("verbose"):
            typer.echo(version.verbose_summary())
        else:
            typer.echo(version.build_summary())
        raise typer.Exit()


def _startup_auto_update(no_update: bool) -> None:
    """Best-effort background auto-update; never raises, never blocks."""
    try:
        updated = update.maybe_auto_update(no_update=no_update, now=time.time())
        if updated is not None:
            typer.echo(f"Updated to v{updated} — takes effect next run")
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return None


@app.callback(invoke_without_command=True)
def main(
    ctx: typer.Context,
    version: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--version", callback=_version_callback, help="Show version"
    ),
    verbose: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--verbose",
        is_eager=True,
        help="Show verbose version information (with --version)",
    ),
    backend: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--backend", help="Backend to use: local (SQLite) | mcp (remote server)."
    ),
    db: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--db", help="Path to the local SQLite database (local backend)."
    ),
    mcp_url: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--mcp-url", help="MCP server URL (mcp backend)."),
    no_update: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-update", help="Disable the startup update check"),
) -> None:  # noqa: B008
    context.set_options(backend=backend, db_path=db, mcp_url=mcp_url)
    if not no_update:
        threading.Thread(target=_startup_auto_update, args=(no_update,), daemon=True).start()

    if ctx.invoked_subcommand is None:
        # No subcommand: start the conversational experience when attached to a
        # terminal, otherwise print help so pipes and CI never block on a prompt.
        if sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty():
            from agentic_odi_cli.chat import ChatConfig, run_chat

            run_chat(ChatConfig.from_env())
        else:
            typer.echo(ctx.get_help())

def _reexec_current() -> None:
    """Re-exec into the freshly installed binary (POSIX only)."""
    current = paths.current_link()
    binary = current / "odi"
    can_exec = (
        os.name == "posix" and hasattr(os, "execv") and current.is_symlink() and binary.exists()
    )
    if not can_exec:
        typer.echo("Update applied; it will take effect on the next run.")
        return
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if "update" in argv:
        argv = argv[: argv.index("update")]
    os.execv(str(binary), [str(binary), *argv])  # nosec B606 - re-execs own verified binary


@app.command(name="schema")
def schema_cmd() -> None:
    """Print the canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity."""
    typer.echo(json.dumps(run_tool("get_odi_schema", {}), indent=2))


@app.command(name="evaluate")
def evaluate_cmd(
    statement: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Outcome statement to check"),
    job_id: str | None = typer.Option(default=None, help="Job to compare against"),
    json_output: bool = typer.Option(False, "--json", help="Emit machine-readable JSON."),
) -> None:
    """Check whether a statement reads as a well-formed ODI desired outcome."""
    args: dict[str, object] = {"statement": statement}
    if job_id is not None:
        args["job_id"] = job_id
    result = run_tool("evaluate_outcome", args)
    if json_output:
        typer.echo(result if isinstance(result, str) else json.dumps(result))
        return
    parsed = json.loads(result) if isinstance(result, str) else result
    verdict = "passes" if parsed.get("valid") else "needs work"
    typer.echo(f"{verdict}: {statement}")
    for problem in parsed.get("issues", []):
        typer.echo(f"  - {problem}")


@app.command(name="guidelines")

@app.command(name="version")
def version_cmd() -> None:

    typer.echo(version.build_summary())


@app.command(name="update")
def update_cmd(
    check: bool = False,
    force: bool = False,
    version: str | None = None,
    now: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Check for or apply CLI updates."""
    if check:
        latest = update.latest_release(__version__)
        if latest is None:
            typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
        else:
            typer.echo(f"Update available: v{latest} - run 'odi update' to install.")
        return

    if not paths.is_frozen():
        typer.echo("This is a source install; use your package manager to update.")
        return

    target = version.lstrip("v") if version else update.latest_release(__version__)
    if target is None:
        if force:
            target = __version__
        else:
            typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
            return

    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
            archive = update.download(target, Path(tmp))
            digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        typer.echo(f"Update failed: {exc}", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc

    typer.echo(f"Updated to v{target}")
    if now:
        _reexec_current()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

588: def _parse_remote(tool_name: str, text: str) -> Any:
589:     """Parse a tool result, raising ``BackendError`` on the server's error text."""
590:     from agentic_odi_core.remote import parse_tool_result
591: 
592:     stripped = text.strip()
593:     problem = parse_tool_result(stripped)
594:     if problem is not None:
595:         raise BackendError(problem.message)

597:     if tool_name in _FLOAT_TOOLS:
598:         return _extract_float(stripped)
599:     if tool_name in _ID_TOOLS:
600:         return stripped.rsplit(": ", 1)[-1]
601: 
602:     payload = _extract_json(stripped)
603:     if tool_name in _LIST_TOOLS and not isinstance(payload, list):
604:         return [payload]
605:     return payload
606: 
607: 
608: def _extract_json(text: str) -> Any:
609:     """Parse the first complete JSON value in ``text``, prose and all.
610: 
611:     MCP replies often wrap a payload in a sentence, and that sentence can
612:     itself contain braces (``created {JOB-1}: [...]``). Each brace is tried as
613:     a start position with ``raw_decode``, so a stray one is skipped instead of
614:     swallowing the real payload, and the outermost value wins when payloads
615:     nest. Text with no parseable value is returned unchanged.
616:     """
617:     decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
618:     for index, char in enumerate(text):
619:         if char not in "{[":
620:             continue
621:         try:
622:             payload, _end = decoder.raw_decode(text, index)
623:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
624:             continue
625:         return payload
626:     return text
627: 
628: 
629: def _extract_float(text: str) -> float:
630:     try:

632:     except ValueError as exc:
633:         raise BackendError(text) from exc

645: ) -> Backend:
646:     resolved = backend or os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND") or DEFAULT_BACKEND

653:

656:         typer.echo("Warning: --db is ignored when the backend is 'mcp'", err=True)
657:     return get_backend(backend=config.backend, db_path=config.db_path, mcp_url=config.mcp_url)
658: 
659: 
660: def require_backend() -> Backend:

664:     return resolve_backend(context.config())

"""Backend abstraction for the CLI.

Two backends implement the same :class:`Backend` seam:

* :class:`LocalBackend` runs the ODI logic directly against a local SQLite
  store (no server required).
* :class:`MCPBackend` delegates to a remote MCP server over HTTP, which may be
  a local ``python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`` process or a hosted endpoint.

Commands resolve a backend once from the options stored on
:mod:`agentic_odi_cli.context`. Keeping the local and remote paths behind one interface
means the same command works against either, and a future hosted backend only
has to implement ``call``.
"""

"""Interactive conversational mode for the Agentic ODI CLI.

The chat is a small terminal REPL around an OpenAI-compatible model and the
Agentic ODI MCP server. It streams assistant text, executes MCP tool calls,

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import traceback
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol

import typer
from agentic_odi_core import ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
from fastmcp import Client
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

from agentic_odi_cli.mascot import render_banner, should_show_banner, wants_color

DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
    + """

You are running in a terminal chat. Use the available MCP tools to create and
query Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes instead of inventing
records or IDs. Follow the ODI outcome statement format and flag opportunity
scores above 10 as underserved. Keep answers concise and readable as plain text.
"""
)

HELP_TEXT = """Commands:
  /help      Show this help
  /status    Show connection status (model, MCP server)
  /connect   Configure LLM provider and MCP server (wizard)
  /model <name>  Switch to a different model
  /mcp <url>     Reconnect to a different MCP server
  /clear     Clear the conversation history
  /tools     List the MCP tools available to the assistant
  /exit      Quit (also /quit)

Anything else is sent to the ODI assistant."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChatConfig:
    """Connection settings for an interactive chat session."""

    base_url: str
    api_key: str
    model: str
    mcp_url: str

    @classmethod
    def from_env(
        cls,
        *,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        mcp_url: str | None = None,
    ) -> ChatConfig:
        """Resolve settings in priority order: explicit arg > env var > LLM profile > default."""
        # Lazy import to avoid circular imports between chat and profile.
        from agentic_odi_cli.profile import load_llm_profile  # noqa: PLC0415

        try:
            llm_profile = load_llm_profile()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            llm_profile = None

        return cls(
            base_url=(
                base_url
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
                or (llm_profile.base_url if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_BASE_URL
            ),
            api_key=(
                api_key
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY")
                or (llm_profile.api_key if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_API_KEY
            ),
            model=(
                model
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL")
                or (llm_profile.model if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_MODEL
            ),
            mcp_url=(
                mcp_url
                or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL")
                or (llm_profile.mcp_url if llm_profile else None)
                or DEFAULT_MCP_URL
            ),
        )


@dataclass
class ConnectionState:
    """Mutable connection status for a chat session."""

    llm_ok: bool = False
    mcp_ok: bool = False
    mcp_tool_count: int = 0
    error_llm: str | None = None
    error_mcp: str | None = None


class ChatSessionLike(Protocol):
    """The session surface the command handler needs."""

    tool_names: list[str]
    config: ChatConfig
    connection_state: ConnectionState

    def clear(self) -> None: ...

    def update_config(self, config: ChatConfig) -> None: ...


def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
    return [
        {
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": tool.name,
                "description": tool.description or "",
                "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
            },
        }
        for tool in tools
    ]


def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
    return [
        {
            "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": entry["name"],
                "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
            },
        }
        for index, entry in entries.items()
    ]


def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
    """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
    content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
    parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
    text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
    return text or str(result)


def handle_command(
    line: str,
    session: ChatSessionLike,
    *,
    on_connect: Callable[[], ChatConfig | None] | None = None,
    on_mcp_reconnect: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None,
) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | tuple[str, str] | None:
    """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message.

    Returns:
        "exit"              — caller should end the session.
        "handled"           — command was handled; continue the REPL.
        ("reconnect_mcp", url) — caller should reconnect MCP then continue.
        None                — not a command; caller should send to the LLM.
    """
    command = line.strip().lower()
    if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
        return "exit"
    if command == "/help":
        typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
        return "handled"
    if command == "/clear":
        session.clear()
        typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
        return "handled"
    if command == "/tools":
        if session.tool_names:
            typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
        else:
            typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
        return "handled"
    if command == "/status":
        state = session.connection_state
        llm_status = "connected" if state.llm_ok else "not connected"
        mcp_status = (
            f"connected ({state.mcp_tool_count} tools)" if state.mcp_ok else "not connected"
        )
        typer.echo(f"model  : {session.config.model}  [{llm_status}]")
        typer.echo(f"url    : {session.config.base_url}")
        typer.echo(f"mcp    : {session.config.mcp_url}  [{mcp_status}]")
        return "handled"
    if command.startswith("/model"):
        parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
        if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
            typer.echo(f"Current model: {session.config.model}")
        else:
            new_model = parts[1].strip()
            new_config = ChatConfig(
                base_url=session.config.base_url,
                api_key=session.config.api_key,
                model=new_model,
                mcp_url=session.config.mcp_url,
            )
            session.update_config(new_config)
            typer.echo(f"Model set to: {new_model}")
        return "handled"
    if command.startswith("/mcp"):
        parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
        if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
            typer.echo(f"Current MCP URL: {session.config.mcp_url}")
        else:
            new_url = parts[1].strip()
            if on_mcp_reconnect is not None:
                ok = on_mcp_reconnect(new_url)
                if ok:
                    typer.echo(
                        f"MCP reconnected: {new_url} ({session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count} tools)"
                    )
                else:
                    typer.echo(f"Failed to connect to MCP at {new_url}")
            else:
                typer.echo("MCP reconnect not available in this context.")
        return "handled"
    if command == "/connect":
        if on_connect is not None:
            connected_config = on_connect()
            if connected_config is not None:
                typer.echo(f"Connected: {connected_config.model} @ {connected_config.base_url}")
        else:
            typer.echo("Connect wizard not available in this context.")
        return "handled"
    if command.startswith("/"):
        typer.echo(f"Unknown command: {line}. Type /help for commands.")
        return "handled"
    return None


async def _try_connect_mcp(mcp_url: str) -> tuple[Any, list[Any], str | None]:
    """Attempt to connect to the MCP server and list its tools.

    Returns:
        (mcp_client, tools, None) on success.
        (None, [], error_message) on failure.
    """
    try:
        async with Client(mcp_url) as c:
            tools = await c.list_tools()
        # Re-create a fresh context manager for the caller to manage lifetime.
        return Client(mcp_url), tools, None
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return None, [], str(exc)


class ChatSession:
    """A streamed tool-calling conversation against an OpenAI-compatible model."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: ChatConfig,
        openai_client: Any,
        mcp_client: Any,
        *,
        connection_state: ConnectionState | None = None,
        on_tool: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self.openai_client = openai_client
        self.mcp_client = mcp_client
        self.connection_state = (
            connection_state if connection_state is not None else ConnectionState()
        )
        self.on_tool = on_tool
        self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
        self.tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.tool_names: list[str] = []

    async def initialize(self) -> None:
        """Discover the MCP tools once and expose them to the model."""
        tools = await self.mcp_client.list_tools()
        self.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
        self.tool_names = [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools]

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Drop the conversation history but keep the system prompt and tools."""
        self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]

    def update_config(self, new_config: ChatConfig) -> None:
        """Hot-swap the session config and mark the LLM connection as live."""
        self.config = new_config
        self.connection_state.llm_ok = True

    async def _stream_completion(
        self, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None
    ) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict[str, str]]]:
        stream: Any = await self.openai_client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self.config.model,
            messages=self.messages,
            tools=self.tools or None,
            tool_choice="auto" if self.tools else None,
            stream=True,
        )

        content_parts: list[str] = []
        tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}

        async for chunk in stream:
            choices = getattr(chunk, "choices", None)
            if not choices:
                continue
            delta = choices[0].delta
            if delta is None:
                continue
            content = getattr(delta, "content", None)
            if content:
                content_parts.append(content)
                if on_delta is not None:
                    on_delta(content)
            for tool_call in getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []:
                entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
                    tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
                )
                if tool_call.id:
                    entry["id"] = tool_call.id
                function = getattr(tool_call, "function", None)
                if function is not None:
                    if function.name:
                        entry["name"] = function.name
                    if function.arguments:
                        entry["arguments"] += function.arguments

        return "".join(content_parts), tool_calls

    async def _call_tool(self, call: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        name = call["function"]["name"]
        raw_arguments = call["function"].get("arguments") or "{}"
        try:
            arguments = json.loads(raw_arguments)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return f"Error: invalid JSON arguments for {name}: {raw_arguments}"
        if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
            return f"Error: arguments for {name} must be a JSON object"
        if self.on_tool is not None:
            self.on_tool(name, arguments)
        try:
            result = await self.mcp_client.call_tool(name, arguments)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"Error calling {name}: {exc}"
        return _tool_result_text(result)

    async def ask(self, text: str, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> str:
        """Send a message, execute any tool calls, and return the final text."""
        if not self.connection_state.llm_ok:
            return "No model connected. Type /connect to set one up."

        checkpoint = len(self.messages)
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
        try:
            while True:
                content, tool_calls = await self._stream_completion(on_delta)
                if not tool_calls:
                    self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
                    return content

                normalized = _normalize_tool_calls(tool_calls)
                self.messages.append(
                    {"role": "assistant", "content": content or None, "tool_calls": normalized}
                )
                for call in normalized:
                    result = await self._call_tool(call)
                    self.messages.append(
                        {
                            "role": "tool",
                            "tool_call_id": call["id"],
                            "name": call["function"]["name"],
                            "content": result,
                        }
                    )
        except Exception:
            del self.messages[checkpoint:]
            raise


def _print_tool(name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    rendered = json.dumps(arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
    if len(rendered) > 100:
        rendered = rendered[:97] + "..."
    typer.secho(f"  → {name} {rendered}", fg="bright_black", err=True)


async def _run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> int:
    if should_show_banner(sys.stdout):
        typer.echo(render_banner(color=wants_color()))
    typer.echo("Agentic ODI · interactive")

    llm: Any | None = None
    conn = ConnectionState()

    try:
        # --- MCP connection (optional) ---
        mcp_client_ctx, tools, mcp_error = await _try_connect_mcp(config.mcp_url)
        if mcp_error is None:
            conn.mcp_ok = True
            conn.mcp_tool_count = len(tools)
        else:
            conn.error_mcp = mcp_error
            typer.secho(
                f"⚠  MCP unavailable ({config.mcp_url}): {mcp_error}",
                fg="yellow",
                err=False,
            )
            typer.secho(
                "   Starting without MCP tools. Use /mcp to reconnect.",
                fg="yellow",
                err=False,
            )

        # --- LLM client (always created; actual reachability found on first use) ---
        llm = AsyncOpenAI(
            base_url=config.base_url,
            api_key=config.api_key,
            timeout=60.0,
        )
        conn.llm_ok = True

        # --- Startup banner ---
        mcp_status = f"✓ {conn.mcp_tool_count} tools" if conn.mcp_ok else "✗ offline"
        typer.echo(f"model: {config.model}  ·  mcp: {config.mcp_url} [{mcp_status}]")
        typer.echo("Type /help for commands, /exit to quit.\n")

        # --- Build session ---
        session = ChatSession(
            config,
            llm,
            mcp_client_ctx,  # may be None if MCP is offline
            connection_state=conn,
            on_tool=_print_tool,
        )

        # Populate tools from the probe we already did (avoids a second round-trip).
        if conn.mcp_ok and tools:
            session.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
            session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]

        # --- REPL ---
        while True:
            try:
                line = input("you › ").strip()
            except EOFError:
                typer.echo()
                break
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                typer.echo("\nUse /exit to quit.")
                continue

            if not line:
                continue

            def _on_connect() -> ChatConfig | None:
                from agentic_odi_cli.wizard import run_connect_wizard  # noqa: PLC0415

                new_config = run_connect_wizard(session.config)
                if new_config is not None:
                    session.update_config(new_config)
                return new_config

            def _on_mcp_reconnect(new_url: str) -> bool:
                """Run MCP reconnect in a separate thread (avoids nested event loops)."""
                import concurrent.futures  # noqa: PLC0415

                async def _reconnect() -> bool:
                    _, new_tools, err = await _try_connect_mcp(new_url)
                    if err is not None:
                        return False
                    new_config = ChatConfig(
                        base_url=session.config.base_url,
                        api_key=session.config.api_key,
                        model=session.config.model,
                        mcp_url=new_url,
                    )
                    session.update_config(new_config)
                    session.mcp_client = Client(new_url)
                    session.tools = _to_openai_tools(new_tools)
                    session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]
                    session.connection_state.mcp_ok = True
                    session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count = len(new_tools)
                    return True

                with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
                    future = executor.submit(asyncio.run, _reconnect())
                    return future.result()

            action = handle_command(
                line, session, on_connect=_on_connect, on_mcp_reconnect=_on_mcp_reconnect
            )
            if action == "exit":
                break
            if action == "handled":
                continue

            typer.secho("odi › ", fg="green", bold=True, nl=False)
            printed = False

            def on_delta(piece: str) -> None:
                nonlocal printed
                printed = True
                typer.echo(piece, nl=False)

            try:
                reply = await session.ask(line, on_delta=on_delta)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                typer.echo()
                typer.echo(f"Error: {exc}", err=True)
                if os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_DEBUG"):
                    typer.echo(traceback.format_exc(), err=True)
                continue
            typer.echo()
            if not printed:
                typer.echo(reply if reply else "(no response)")

    finally:
        if llm is not None:
            await llm.close()

    typer.echo("Goodbye.")
    return 0


def run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> None:
    """Run the interactive chat until the user exits."""
    try:
        exit_code = asyncio.run(_run_chat(config))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        typer.echo("\nGoodbye.")
        return
    if exit_code:
        raise typer.Exit(code=exit_code)

"""Connection probing and LLM health checks, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os
import socket
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from openai import AsyncOpenAI

DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"

OFFLINE_MESSAGE = "LLM server offline (Local Studio Mode enabled)"


def _load_profile_fallback() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read llm_profile.json directly without importing cli package."""
    import json
    from pathlib import Path

    xdg = os.getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    cfg_dir = Path(xdg) / "agentic-odi" if xdg else Path.home() / ".config" / "agentic-odi"
    profile_file = cfg_dir / "llm_profile.json"
    if not profile_file.exists():
        return {}
    try:
        with open(profile_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {}


def defaults() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Streamlit-compatible environment defaults (same variable names).

    Priority order: environment variable > persisted llm_profile.json > hardcoded constant.
    """
    profile = _load_profile_fallback()
    return {
        "base_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
        or profile.get("base_url")
        or DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
        "api_key": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY") or profile.get("api_key") or DEFAULT_API_KEY,
        "model_name": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL") or profile.get("model") or DEFAULT_MODEL,
        "mcp_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL") or profile.get("mcp_url") or DEFAULT_MCP_URL,
    }


def is_endpoint_reachable(url: str, timeout: float = 0.3) -> bool:
    """Quick socket check to verify a port is open without hanging on HTTP reads."""
    try:
        parsed = urlparse(url)
        host = parsed.hostname or "localhost"
        port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme == "https" else 80)
        with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
            return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def classify_llm_error(exc: Exception) -> tuple[str, str]:
    message = str(exc)
    lower = message.lower()
    connection_indicators = [
        "connection error",
        "connection aborted",
        "failed to establish a new connection",
        "timed out",
        "timeout",
        "connection refused",
    ]
    if any(indicator in lower for indicator in connection_indicators):
        return "connection_error", message
    return "error", message


async def check_llm_health(base_url: str, api_key: str, model_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Non-blocking LLM health probe with an instant socket pre-check."""
    if not is_endpoint_reachable(base_url, timeout=0.3):
        return False, OFFLINE_MESSAGE

    client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key, timeout=1.2)
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(client.models.list(), timeout=1.2)
        return True, "LLM backend is reachable."
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        status, detail = classify_llm_error(exc)
        return False, f"{status}: {detail}"

750:       const controller = new AbortController();

753:       let content = "";
754:       let parts: ChatPart[] = [];
755:       let failure: StudioError | null = null;
756:       let terminal = false;
757:       let stopped = false;
758: 
759:       // Prose is appended to the open text part; a surface opens a new one, so
760:       // the transcript keeps the agent's order instead of gathering all prose
761:       // above all cards.
762:       const appendText = (text: string) => {
763:         if (!text) {
764:           return;
765:         }
766:         content += text;
767:         const last = parts[parts.length - 1];
768:         parts =
769:           last?.kind === "text"
770:             ? [...parts.slice(0, -1), { kind: "text", text: last.text + text }]
771:             : [...parts, { kind: "text", text }];

774:       const publish = () => {
775:         setMessages((prev) => {
776:           const next = [...prev];

778:             role: "assistant",
779:             content,
780:             parts: [...parts],
781:             ...(failure ? { error: failure, retryText: trimmed } : {}),
782:           };
783:           return next;
784:         });
785:       };
786: 
787:       const handleEvent = (event: RawSseEvent) => {
788:         switch (event.event) {
789:           case "status": {
790:             const phase = String(event.data.phase ?? "");
791:             setThinkingPhase(phase);
792:             if (phase === "offline") {
793:               setOfflineReply(true);
794:             }
795:             break;
796:           }
797:           case "delta": {
798:             appendText(String(event.data.text ?? ""));
799:             publish();
800:             break;
801:           }
802:           case "ui": {
803:             // Validate again on arrival: the connection is local but the
804:             // renderer must never trust a shape it has not checked.
805:             const parsed = parseUiSpec(event.data.spec, catalogManifest());
806:             if (parsed.ok) {
807:               parts = [
808:                 ...parts,
809:                 { kind: "ui", id: String(event.data.id ?? `ui-${parts.length}`), node: parsed.node },
810:               ];
811:               publish();
812:             }
813:             break;
814:           }
815:           case "tool":
816:             setToolActivity((prev) => [
817:               ...prev,
818:               {
819:                 name: String(event.data.name ?? ""),
820:                 status: String(event.data.status ?? ""),
821:                 preview: event.data.preview ? String(event.data.preview) : undefined,
822:               },
823:             ]);
824:             break;
825:           case "message": {
826:             terminal = true;
827:             content = String(event.data.content ?? content);
828:             const hasSurfaces = parts.some((part) => part.kind === "ui");
829:             if (!hasSurfaces) {
830:               parts = content ? [{ kind: "text", text: content }] : [];
831:             }
832:             publish();
833:             break;
834:           }
835:           case "conversation": {
836:             const id = String(event.data.id ?? "");
837:             if (id) {
838:               setConversationId(id);
839:             }
840:             break;
841:           }
842:           case "memory": {
843:             const observation = event.data.observation as Observation | undefined;
844:             if (observation?.id) {
845:               setMemory((prev) =>
846:                 prev.some((item) => item.id === observation.id)
847:                   ? prev.map((item) => (item.id === observation.id ? observation : item))
848:                   : [...prev, observation],
849:               );
850:             }
851:             break;
852:           }
853:           case "canvas_dirty":
854:             void refreshCanvas();
855:             break;
856:           case "connector": {
857:             if (String(event.data.status ?? "") === "error") {
858:               const reason = String(event.data.error ?? "The connector could not be added.");
859:               setMessages((prev) => [
860:                 ...prev,
861:                 { role: "notice", content: `Connector failed: ${reason}` },
862:               ]);
863:             } else {
864:               setConnectorSuggestions((prev) => {
865:                 const id = String(event.data?.preset ?? event.data?.name ?? "");
866:                 if (!id || prev.includes(id)) {
867:                   return prev;
868:                 }
869:                 return [...prev, id];
870:               });
871:             }
872:             void refreshConnectors();
873:             break;
874:           }
875:           case "error": {
876:             terminal = true;
877:             failure = readStudioError(event.data.error);
878:             publish();
879:             break;
880:           }
881:           default:
882:             break;
883:         }
884:       };
885: 
886:       try {
887:         await streamChat(
888:           {
889:             base_url: settings.base_url,
890:             api_key: settings.api_key,
891:             model: settings.model_name,
892:             mcp_url: settings.mcp_url,
893:             messages: history,
894:             brief,
895:             ui_catalog: catalogManifest(),
896:             conversation_id: conversationId,

899:           controller.signal,

903:         if (aborted) {
904:           // An abort is the user's own doing: drop the empty placeholder, keep
905:           // the question, and report no failure — the assistant did not break.
906:           stopped = true;
907:           setMessages((prev) => {
908:             const next = [...prev];
909:             if (next.length && next[next.length - 1].role === "assistant" && !next[next.length - 1].content) {
910:               next.pop();
911:             }
912:             return next;
