 # Running The Living Studio
 
 **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
 an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
 Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
 connected to the MCP server.
 
 The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve
 the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the
 SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```text
 ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
 │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
 │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
 │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
 └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                              │  - conversations + PM memory  │
                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                              ▼
                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                              │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                              ▲
                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
 ```
 
 ## Interface
 
 The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.
 
 | Surface | What it does |
 |---|---|
 | **First-run tour** | A four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which ambition brought you here, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. The four doors are **I have one in mind**, **My boss handed me a priority**, **Help me find the next one**, and **Pressure-test a bet**; each starts the matching conversation. Replay it from **Settings → Replay the welcome tour**. |
 | **First run** | A short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and **Explore on my own** always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with `/start`, the home stage's context pill, or Settings. |
 | **Hero** | One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or an intent-first prompt such as *What are you trying to win this quarter?* It cycles every few seconds and stays still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
 | **Suggestion pills** | Below the headline. **Sharpen an opportunity** always starts a conversation; the next pill becomes **Pressure-test a bet** once outcomes exist, or **Find the next opportunity** before that. **Capture what you heard** replaces the landscape pill once a job exists. They change as the canvas fills up. |
 | **Composer** | Docked at the bottom of the transcript. `Enter` sends, `Shift`+`Enter` adds a line, `Cmd/Ctrl`+`K` focuses it, and `/` opens the command palette. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams. |
 | **Bar** | The only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread. |
 | **Rail** | Above the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: `Landscape · N`, `Job map · N`, `Evidence · N`, `What I know · N`. Every item is derived from the canvas and the memory, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu. |
 | **Lens** | A view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. The transcript and the composer stay on screen and stay usable; `Esc`, **Close**, or the rail chip closes it. Every lens ends in one sentence that re-enters the conversation — *Ask which to chase*, *Walk me through the job*, *Weigh the evidence* — so leaving a view is never a return to a menu. Settings and catch-up use the same lens. |
 
 Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code).
 Tool calls appear inline as small trace chips while the agent works.
 
 ### Slash commands
 
 Type `/` to open the palette. `Up`/`Down` move, `Enter` or `Tab` runs the
 selected command, `Esc` closes it. Commands are handled in the SPA and never call
 the model, so they work when it is offline.
 
 | Command | Effect |
 |---|---|
 | `/help` | Every command, as a notice in the transcript |
 | `/start` | Resume the context conversation |
 | `/new` | New conversation |
 | `/home` | Return to the empty stage |
 | `/jobs` | Job summary, then the job map |
 | `/landscape`, `/jobmap`, `/evidence`, `/settings` | Open that lens beside the conversation |
 | `/impact`, `/capture` | Start the conversation that produces the card. `/capture` falls back to the offline form when no model answers. |
 | `/status` | Model, MCP, context, and canvas status |
 
 Unknown commands produce a transcript notice pointing at `/help`.
 
 ### The welcome tour
 
 The tour is the front door, the context conversation is the first room. It is
 skippable at every step (`Skip the tour` or `Escape`), resumable (progress is
 stored after every transition in `localStorage["studio.onboarding"]`), and
 replayable from Settings.
 
 Everything lives in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/`:
 
 | File | Role |
 |---|---|
 | `content.ts` | Steps and goal copy as typed data — the only place the words live |
 | `machine.ts` | Pure state transitions, no React or storage |
 | `storage.ts` | Versioned, defensive `localStorage` persistence |
 | `OnboardingProvider.tsx` | Auto-open, persistence, replay |
 | `FirstRunWizard.tsx`, `steps.tsx`, `onboarding.css` | The dialog |
 | `../features/flags.ts` | The `firstRunWizard` toggle |
 
 `App.tsx` only wires the provider and the wizard around the existing shell;
 the chat, canvas, and sidecar code are untouched.
 
 #### Toggling the tour
 
 `firstRunWizard` defaults to on. Resolution order, highest first:
 
 | Source | Example | Use |
 |---|---|---|
 | Query parameter | `?flags=firstRunWizard:off` | QA a build without rebuilding |
 | Local override | `localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"] = "off"` | Per-browser opt-out |
 | Build environment | `VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD=off npm --prefix apps/studio run build` | Ship it dark |
 | Default | on | |
 
 Accepted values are `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`, and
 `enabled`/`disabled`. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state
 is written, and Settings hides the replay action.
 
 ### Guidance, not gates
 
 The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the
 home stage keeps a dashed **Tell me what you're building** pill; it reopens the
 conversation exactly where you left off. `/start` and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a
 natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts
 instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review
 and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.
 
 ### Without a model
 
 When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:
 
 - A **Working by hand** strip explains the state and offers capture, job map,
   and context.
 - Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled
   **Local guidance**.
 - Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed;
   outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same
   local repository the model uses.
 - Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.
 
 The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
 the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.

 ### The thread is the room
 
 Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront
 never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the
 customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that
 carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for
 doing the work.
 
 That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every
 artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each
 reply with the next move as an action on the surface.
 
 ### What it remembers
 
 The studio keeps a small, local, editable model of the person it is helping. It
 is not a profile and not a transcript index; it is the handful of things that
 change the next answer.
 
 | Kind | What it captures |
 |---|---|
 | `career` | The PM's role, remit, and what success looks like for them |
 | `opportunity` | The opportunity or bet currently in play |
 | `business` | Goals, metrics, and commercial constraints |
 | `stakeholder` | Who else matters and what they care about |
 | `constraint` | Time, budget, policy, or technical limits |
 | `evidence` | What has actually been heard or measured |
 | `preference` | How the PM likes to work and be spoken to |
 
 Each note is `suggested` or `confirmed`. Suggested notes appear first under
 **What I know** with **Yes, that's right**, **That's not it**, and **Edit**;
 confirmed notes can be edited or forgotten. The PM can also add a note by hand.
 Nothing is silently promoted: the agent may propose, but the person decides.
 
 The agent writes notes through a `remember` tool during a normal reply. The
 sidecar applies it, emits a `memory` SSE event, and the panel updates without a
 refresh. Memory writes are best-effort — a database failure never turns a good
 answer into an error.
 
 Storage is a separate SQLite file from the ODI repository:
 `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`
 (`:memory:` is supported and is what the tests use). The API is small:
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/api/memory/observations` | Everything the agent believes |
 | `POST` | `/api/memory/observations` | Add a note by hand |
 | `PATCH` | `/api/memory/observations/{id}` | Edit text, confidence, or status |
 | `DELETE` | `/api/memory/observations/{id}` | Forget one note |
 | `DELETE` | `/api/memory` | Forget all notes and conversations |
 
 **Forget everything** is a two-step confirmation and also clears the visible
 thread, because the server deletes the conversations behind it.
 
 ### The thread comes back
 
 Conversations are stored beside the memory. On launch the SPA asks
 `GET /api/conversations/latest`, restores that thread's user and assistant
 turns, and continues with the same `conversation_id` on the next message. **New
 conversation** starts a fresh one without touching the memory; **Forget
 everything** removes both. The composer stays usable while the restore is in
 flight, and a restore failure simply leaves the room empty.
 
 ## Rich responses
 
 The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
 paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
 outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a
 customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, an opportunity thesis, or a decision record.
 Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:
 
 - **The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA.**
   `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` declares nine primitives and seven cards, their
   JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no
   eval, and no third-party component in the path. Prose is rendered by the same
   `Markdown` component the transcript already used.
 - **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;
   the sidecar derives the `render_ui` tool schema from it, validates what comes
   back, and streams a `ui` SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool
   result naming the exact violation, and the loop offers the tool again, so a
   fumbled prop is corrected in the same reply. A client that sends no catalog
   never sees the tool.
 - **Cards are views, never actors.** Every button is an `intent` string that the
   agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.
 
 A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:
 
 ```json
 {
   "type": "outcome-card",
   "props": {
     "id": "O-1",
     "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
     "importance": 9,
     "satisfaction": 3
   }
 }
 ```
 
 The opportunity thesis is the intent-first card: one opportunity with its
 importance, satisfaction, the gap in plain words, the thesis itself, and the
 smallest next move. It is the shape the agent reaches for when the PM is deciding
 what to chase, rather than when they are inspecting a single score.
 
 The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a `delta` appends to the
 open prose part, a `ui` event opens a card, and the next `delta` opens a new
 paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and
 satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home
 (`src/lib/odi.ts`). Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree
 that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.
 
 ### Adding a surface
 
 1. Add an entry to `CATALOG` in `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — props as a
    JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
 2. Register the component in `apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts`.
 3. Implement it in `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx` (domain shape) or
    `apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx` (composition).
 4. Run `npm --prefix apps/studio test`. The `registry parity` test fails if the
    catalog and the registry drift apart.
 
 No server change is needed, and no new dependency.

 ## Desktop signing & updater secrets
 
 Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
 unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
 Actions secrets.
 
 | Secret | Purpose |
 |---|---|
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate`. |
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
 | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
 | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
 | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
 | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |
 
 Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
 is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
 **Settings → Check for updates**.
 
 ### Managing the updater signing key
 
 The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
 verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
 embedded in `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
 safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
 CI, or attached to a build artifact.
 
 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
    passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:
 
    ```bash
    npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
    ```
 
    This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
    (public).
 
 2. **Paste the public key** into `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:
 
    ```jsonc
    {
      "plugins": {
        "updater": {
          "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
          "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
 
 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
    git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:
 
    ```bash
    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
    mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
    chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    ```
 
    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
    Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
    Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
    installs.
 
 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
    variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:
 
    ```bash
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
    ```
 
 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):
 
    ```bash
    gh secret list
    ```
 
 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
    new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
    their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
    key ahead of the cut-over.
 
 > [!CAUTION]
 > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
 > pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.
 
 ## Connecting an LLM
 
 The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
 drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
 [Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).
 
 ## Agent-Driven Testing
 
 Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
 both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.
 
 Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
 automatically.

Running The Living Studio

The chat-first interface, its first run, and the desktop app.

The Living Studio is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation: an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent connected to the MCP server.

The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on http://127.0.0.1:8100 — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.

Architecture

┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
 │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
 │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
 │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
 └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                              │  - conversations + PM memory  │
                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                              ▼
                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                              │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                              ▲
                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │

Interface

The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.

Surface What it does
First-run tour A four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which ambition brought you here, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. The four doors are I have one in mind, My boss handed me a priority, Help me find the next one, and Pressure-test a bet; each starts the matching conversation. Replay it from Settings → Replay the welcome tour.
First run A short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and Explore on my own always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with /start, the home stage's context pill, or Settings.
Hero One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or an intent-first prompt such as What are you trying to win this quarter? It cycles every few seconds and stays still under prefers-reduced-motion.
Suggestion pills Below the headline. Sharpen an opportunity always starts a conversation; the next pill becomes Pressure-test a bet once outcomes exist, or Find the next opportunity before that. Capture what you heard replaces the landscape pill once a job exists. They change as the canvas fills up.
Composer Docked at the bottom of the transcript. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, Cmd/Ctrl+K focuses it, and / opens the command palette. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams.
Bar The only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread.
Rail Above the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: Landscape · N, Job map · N, Evidence · N, What I know · N. Every item is derived from the canvas and the memory, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu.
Lens A view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. The transcript and the composer stay on screen and stay usable; Esc, Close, or the rail chip closes it. Every lens ends in one sentence that re-enters the conversation — Ask which to chase, Walk me through the job, Weigh the evidence — so leaving a view is never a return to a menu. Settings and catch-up use the same lens.

Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code). Tool calls appear inline as small trace chips while the agent works.

/start Resume the context conversation

/impact, /capture Start the conversation that produces the card. /capture falls back to the offline form when no model answers.

  • Cards are views, never actors. Every button is an intent string that the agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.

A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:

{
   "type": "outcome-card",
   "props": {
     "id": "O-1",
     "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
     "importance": 9,
     "satisfaction": 3
   }
 }

The opportunity thesis is the intent-first card: one opportunity with its importance, satisfaction, the gap in plain words, the thesis itself, and the smallest next move. It is the shape the agent reaches for when the PM is deciding what to chase, rather than when they are inspecting a single score.

The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a delta appends to the open prose part, a ui event opens a card, and the next delta opens a new paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home (src/lib/odi.ts). Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.

Adding a surface

  1. Add an entry to CATALOG in apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts — props as a JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
  2. Register the component in apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts.
  3. Implement it in apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx (domain shape) or apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx (composition).
  4. Run npm --prefix apps/studio test. The registry parity test fails if the catalog and the registry drift apart.

No server change is needed, and no new dependency.

Hosted (experimental)

The built SPA is also served from Cloudflare Workers at https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/. The UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the local sidecar and MCP server. Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. See Deployment for the Worker setup.

1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)

npm --prefix apps/studio run build   # build the SPA into apps/studio/dist
 python scripts/dev.py            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
Service URL
MCP Server http://localhost:8000/mcp
Living Studio http://127.0.0.1:8100

python scripts/dev.py starts both processes concurrently; press Ctrl+C to stop both.

2. Web — dev with hot reload

Vite proxies /api to the sidecar:

npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
 # open http://localhost:5173

3. Desktop — Tauri 2

The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:

npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev     # dev window
 npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)

[!NOTE] Tauri prerequisites. The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:

sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64

The Tauri CLI ships as the @tauri-apps/cli npm dev dependency (npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri). The sidecar is launched with uv run python -m … from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the repo root, set AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT.

Desktop signing & updater secrets

Self-updating and code signing are env-driven: if a secret is absent, an unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub Actions secrets.

Secret Purpose
TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY Signs updater artifacts (.sig) and the latest.json manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate.
TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD Password for the private key (optional when the key has none).
APPLE_CERTIFICATE / APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 .p12) and its password.
APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY macOS signing identity.
APPLE_ID / APPLE_PASSWORD / APPLE_TEAM_ID macOS notarization credentials.
WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE / WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config.

Releases are published by .github/workflows/tauri-release.yml when a v* tag is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via Settings → Check for updates.

Managing the updater signing key

The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The public key is embedded in apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (plugins.updater.pubkey) and is safe to commit. The private key must never be committed, logged, printed in CI, or attached to a build artifact.

  1. Generate a key pair (only if you need a new one). Leave -p "" for a passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:

    npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f

    This writes living-studio.key (private, 0600) and living-studio.key.pub (public).

  2. Paste the public key into apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:

    {
   "plugins": {
     "updater": {
       "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
       "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
     }
   }
 }

  3. Store the private key outside the repository (the repo root is git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:

    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
 mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
 chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key

    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/ Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives. Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing installs.

  4. Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:

    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
 gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password

  5. Verify the secrets exist (values are never displayed):

    gh secret list

  6. Rotate by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public key ahead of the cut-over.

[!CAUTION] If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.

Connecting an LLM

The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see Local LLM Backend.

Type /dev in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.

Type /test to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically.

"""Backend abstraction for the CLI.

Two backends implement the same :class:`Backend` seam:

* :class:`LocalBackend` runs the ODI logic directly against a local SQLite
  store (no server required).
* :class:`MCPBackend` delegates to a remote MCP server over HTTP, which may be
  a local ``python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`` process or a hosted endpoint.

Commands resolve a backend once from the options stored on
:mod:`agentic_odi_cli.context`. Keeping the local and remote paths behind one interface
means the same command works against either, and a future hosted backend only
has to implement ``call``.
"""

"""Backend seam: local SQLite backend and remote MCP backend."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from agentic_odi_cli import backend as backend_module
from agentic_odi_cli.backend import (
    BackendConfig,
    BackendError,
    LocalBackend,
    MCPBackend,
    get_backend,
    mcp_timeout,
    resolve_backend,
)

CUSTOMER_VALUE = {
    "direction": "minimize",
    "unit_of_measure": "time",
    "object_of_control": "to resolve setup errors",
    "statement": "Minimize the time to resolve setup errors",
    "importance": 8.8,
    "satisfaction": 3.2,
}
BUSINESS_VALUE = {"category": "cost_reduction", "statement": "Saves engineering hours"}


def _seed_job(backend: LocalBackend, job_id: str = "job-1") -> None:
    """Customer Outcomes validate their parent Job, so seed one first."""
    from agentic_odi_core import Job

    backend.service.repo.add_job(Job(id=job_id, name="Onboard customers"))


def _add_args(job_id: str = "job-1") -> dict:
    return {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "customer_value": dict(CUSTOMER_VALUE),
        "business_value": dict(BUSINESS_VALUE),
    }


def test_local_backend_round_trips_customer_outcomes(tmp_path):
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
    _seed_job(backend)

    created = backend.call("add_customer_outcome", _add_args())
    outcome_id = created["id"]

    fetched = backend.call("get_customer_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id})
    assert fetched["id"] == outcome_id
    assert fetched["customer_value"]["importance"] == 8.8

    listed = backend.call("list_customer_outcomes", {"job_id": "job-1"})
    assert [item["id"] for item in listed] == [outcome_id]

    deleted = backend.call("delete_customer_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id})
    assert deleted == outcome_id
    assert backend.call("list_customer_outcomes", {}) == []


def test_local_update_changes_nested_business_and_customer_value(tmp_path):
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
    _seed_job(backend)
    outcome_id = backend.call("add_customer_outcome", _add_args())["id"]

    updated = backend.call(
        "update_customer_outcome",
        {
            "outcome_id": outcome_id,
            "importance": 9.5,
            "business_statement": "Reduces churn",
        },
    )

    assert updated["customer_value"]["importance"] == 9.5
    assert updated["business_value"]["statement"] == "Reduces churn"
    assert updated["business_value"]["category"] == "cost_reduction"


def test_local_get_missing_raises_backend_error(tmp_path):
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))

    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="Customer outcome not found: nope"):
        backend.call("get_customer_outcome", {"outcome_id": "nope"})


def test_local_backend_defers_database_creation_until_first_call(tmp_path):
    db_path = tmp_path / "odi.db"
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(db_path))

    assert not db_path.exists()
    backend.call("compute_opportunity", {"importance": 8, "satisfaction": 2})
    assert not db_path.exists(), "score must not open the store"


def test_local_compute_opportunity(tmp_path):
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
    assert backend.call("compute_opportunity", {"importance": 8, "satisfaction": 2}) == 14.0


def test_resolve_backend_selects_local_by_default(tmp_path):
    backend = resolve_backend(BackendConfig(backend="local", db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db")))
    assert isinstance(backend, LocalBackend)


def test_get_backend_rejects_unknown_backend():
    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="unknown backend: warp"):
        get_backend(backend="warp")


def test_mcp_timeout_reads_env(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_TIMEOUT", "5.5")
    assert mcp_timeout() == 5.5
    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_TIMEOUT", "nonsense")
    assert mcp_timeout() == 30.0


def test_mcp_backend_parses_list_payload(monkeypatch):
    backend = MCPBackend(mcp_url="http://example/mcp")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "agentic_odi_cli.backend._call_mcp",
        lambda tool, args, url, timeout: '[{"id": "a"}]',
    )
    assert backend.call("list_customer_outcomes", {}) == [{"id": "a"}]


def test_mcp_backend_extracts_model_from_success_text(monkeypatch):
    backend = MCPBackend(mcp_url="http://example/mcp")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "agentic_odi_cli.backend._call_mcp",
        lambda tool, args, url, timeout: 'Customer outcome created successfully: {"id": "a"}',
    )
    assert backend.call("add_customer_outcome", {}) == {"id": "a"}


def test_mcp_backend_treats_not_found_text_as_error(monkeypatch):
    backend = MCPBackend(mcp_url="http://example/mcp")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "agentic_odi_cli.backend._call_mcp",
        lambda tool, args, url, timeout: "Customer outcome not found: gone",
    )
    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="Customer outcome not found: gone"):
        backend.call("get_customer_outcome", {"outcome_id": "gone"})


def test_mcp_backend_parses_opportunity_score(monkeypatch):
    backend = MCPBackend(mcp_url="http://example/mcp")
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "agentic_odi_cli.backend._call_mcp",
        lambda tool, args, url, timeout: "Opportunity score: 14.00",
    )
    assert backend.call("compute_opportunity", {"importance": 8, "satisfaction": 2}) == 14.0


def test_mcp_backend_reports_unreachable_server(monkeypatch):
    """An unreachable server must surface as a clear BackendError.

    The transport is stubbed: dialing a real port makes this test depend on
    whether the host refuses or silently drops the connection, which decided
    between the connection-failure and timeout messages on different runners.
    """

    class _UnreachableClient:
        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            pass

        async def __aenter__(self):
            raise ConnectionError("connection refused")

        async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
            return False

    monkeypatch.setattr("fastmcp.Client", _UnreachableClient)

    backend = MCPBackend(mcp_url="http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp", timeout=0.5)
    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="could not reach MCP server"):
        backend.call("get_customer_outcome", {"outcome_id": "x"})


def test_local_backend_job_step_outcome_crud(tmp_path):
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
    job_id = backend.call("add_job", {"name": "J", "description": "d"})["id"]

    assert backend.call("get_jobs", {})[0]["name"] == "J"
    assert backend.call("get_job", {"job_id": job_id})["name"] == "J"
    assert backend.call("update_job", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "J2"})["name"] == "J2"

    step_id = backend.call("add_step", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "S", "order": 1})["id"]
    assert [step["name"] for step in backend.call("get_job_map", {"job_id": job_id})] == ["S"]
    assert backend.call("update_step", {"step_id": step_id, "name": "S2"})["name"] == "S2"
    assert backend.call("get_step", {"step_id": step_id})["order"] == 1

    outcome_id = backend.call(
        "add_outcome",
        {"job_id": job_id, "statement": "Min x", "importance": 8.0, "satisfaction": 4.0},
    )["id"]
    assert backend.call("get_outcomes", {"job_id": job_id})[0]["statement"] == "Min x"
    updated = backend.call("update_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id, "importance": 9.0})
    assert updated["importance"] == 9.0
    assert backend.call("get_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id})["opportunity_score"] == 14.0

    assert backend.call("delete_step", {"step_id": step_id}) == step_id
    assert backend.call("delete_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id}) == outcome_id
    assert backend.call("delete_job", {"job_id": job_id}) == job_id
    assert backend.call("get_jobs", {}) == []


def test_local_backend_not_found_raises_backend_error(tmp_path):
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))

    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="Job not found: missing"):
        backend.call("get_job", {"job_id": "missing"})
    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="Job not found: missing"):
        backend.call("get_job_map", {"job_id": "missing"})
    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="Step not found: missing"):
        backend.call("get_step", {"step_id": "missing"})
    with pytest.raises(BackendError, match="Outcome not found: missing"):
        backend.call("get_outcome", {"outcome_id": "missing"})


def test_local_backend_rejects_out_of_range_scores(tmp_path):
    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))

display.text:
"""HTTP error shape, status mapping, and request-id correlation."""

from __future__ import annotations

from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
from agentic_odi_core.repository import InMemoryRepository
from agentic_odi_studio_api.app import create_app
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import StudioHTTPError
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient


def _client(app: FastAPI) -> TestClient:
    return TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)


def test_unknown_api_route_returns_the_error_shape() -> None:
    client = _client(create_app(InMemoryRepository()))

    response = client.get("/api/does-not-exist")

    assert response.status_code == 404
    body = response.json()
    assert body["error"]["code"] == "not_found"
    assert body["error"]["request_id"]
    assert response.headers["X-Request-ID"] == body["error"]["request_id"]


def test_validation_failure_returns_the_error_shape() -> None:
    client = _client(create_app(InMemoryRepository()))

    response = client.post("/api/jobs", json={})

    assert response.status_code == 422
    body = response.json()
    assert body["error"]["code"] == "validation"
    assert body["error"]["detail"]
    assert body["error"]["suggestion"] == "Check the request body and try again."


def test_studio_http_error_keeps_its_code_and_status() -> None:
    app = create_app(InMemoryRepository())

    @app.get("/api/boom")
    def boom():
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE, message="out of range")
        )

    response = _client(app).get("/api/boom")

    assert response.status_code == 422
    body = response.json()
    assert body["error"]["code"] == "out_of_range"
    assert body["error"]["message"] == "out of range"


def test_request_id_header_is_echoed() -> None:
    client = _client(create_app(InMemoryRepository()))

    response = client.get("/health", headers={"X-Request-ID": "test-123"})

    assert response.headers["X-Request-ID"] == "test-123"


def test_unhandled_exception_returns_the_error_shape() -> None:
    app = create_app(InMemoryRepository())

    @app.get("/api/kaput")
    def kaput():
        raise RuntimeError("secret internal detail")

    response = _client(app).get("/api/kaput")

    assert response.status_code == 500
    body = response.json()
    assert body["error"]["code"] == "internal"
    assert body["error"]["request_id"]
    assert response.headers["X-Request-ID"] == body["error"]["request_id"]
    assert "secret internal detail" not in response.text


def test_unhandled_exception_surfaces_the_request_id_in_the_message() -> None:
    app = create_app(InMemoryRepository())

    @app.get("/api/kaput")
    def kaput():
        raise RuntimeError("secret internal detail")

    response = _client(app).get("/api/kaput", headers={"X-Request-ID": "req-9"})

    body = response.json()
    assert "req-9" in body["error"]["message"]
    assert body["error"]["message"].startswith("Something went wrong")


def test_unknown_api_route_is_not_swallowed_by_the_spa(monkeypatch, tmp_path) -> None:
    from agentic_odi_studio_api import app as app_module

    (tmp_path / "index.html").write_text("<html>studio</html>")
    monkeypatch.setattr(app_module, "SPA_DIST", tmp_path)

    response = _client(create_app(InMemoryRepository())).get("/api/does-not-exist")

    assert response.status_code == 404
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_found"


def test_chat_request_id_comes_from_the_header_not_the_body() -> None:
    client = _client(create_app(InMemoryRepository()))

    response = client.post(
        "/api/chat",
        json={
            "base_url": "http://llm/v1",
            "api_key": "k",
            "model": "m",
            "mcp_url": "http://mcp",
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
            "request_id": "client-supplied",  # ignored: the header owns the id
        },
        headers={"X-Request-ID": "header-id"},
    )

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.headers["X-Request-ID"] == "header-id"
    assert "client-supplied" not in response.text
    assert "header-id" in response.text


def test_an_unusable_request_id_is_replaced() -> None:
    client = _client(create_app(InMemoryRepository()))

    response = client.get(
        "/api/does-not-exist",
        headers={"X-Request-ID": "a" * 300},
    )

    assert response.status_code == 404
    body = response.json()
    assert body["error"]["request_id"] != "a" * 300
    assert body["error"]["request_id"] == response.headers["X-Request-ID"]


def test_the_spa_fallback_404_body_carries_the_request_id() -> None:
    from agentic_odi_studio_api import app as app_module

    client = _client(create_app(InMemoryRepository()))
    response = client.get("/api/does-not-exist", headers={"X-Request-ID": "req-9"})

    assert response.status_code == 404
    assert response.json()["error"]["request_id"] == "req-9"
    assert app_module is not None

display.text:
"""HTTP error shape, status mapping, and request-id handling for the sidecar.

Every failure the Studio API reports travels as one body::

    {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "detail": ..., "suggestion": ...,
               "retryable": ..., "request_id": ...}}

The model itself lives in :mod:`agentic_odi_core.remote` so the CLI and the
sidecar agree on what a failure is; this module owns the HTTP mapping.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4

from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.datastructures import Headers, MutableHeaders
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID"

#: A request id is echoed in responses and written to logs, so it must be a
#: short, boring token. Anything else is replaced with a fresh one.
REQUEST_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$")

STATUS_FOR_CODE: dict[StudioErrorCode, int] = {
    StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND: 404,
    StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION: 422,
    StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE: 422,
    StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT: 409,
    StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE: 502,
    StudioErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 502,
    StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED: 500,
    StudioErrorCode.LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED: 500,
    StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL: 500,
}

CODE_FOR_STATUS: dict[int, StudioErrorCode] = {
    400: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
    404: StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
    409: StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT,
    422: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
    500: StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
    502: StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
}


class StudioHTTPError(Exception):
    """A failure that already knows its HTTP status and its error model."""

    def __init__(self, error: StudioError, status_code: int | None = None) -> None:
        self.error = error
        self.status_code = status_code if status_code is not None else status_for_code(error.code)
        super().__init__(error.message)


def status_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode) -> int:
    """Return the HTTP status that belongs to an error code."""
    return STATUS_FOR_CODE.get(code, 500)


def code_for_status(status_code: int) -> StudioErrorCode:
    """Return the error code that belongs to an HTTP status."""
    return CODE_FOR_STATUS.get(status_code, StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL)


def request_id_for(request: Request) -> str:
    """Return the request id assigned to this request, or an empty string."""
    return str(getattr(request.state, "request_id", "") or "")


def _error_body(request: Request, error: StudioError) -> dict[str, Any]:
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    if not error.request_id:
        error = error.model_copy(update={"request_id": request_id})
    return {"error": error.model_dump(mode="json")}


def _error_response(request: Request, error: StudioError, status_code: int) -> JSONResponse:
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    headers = {REQUEST_ID_HEADER: request_id} if request_id else None
    return JSONResponse(_error_body(request, error), status_code=status_code, headers=headers)


def studio_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StudioHTTPError) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a :class:`StudioHTTPError` as the one error body."""
    return _error_response(request, exc.error, exc.status_code)


def validation_error_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a request-body validation failure as a ``validation`` error."""
    detail = _compact_validation_text(exc)
    error = StudioError(
        code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
        message="Request validation failed.",
        detail=detail,
        suggestion="Check the request body and try again.",
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, 422)


def _compact_validation_text(exc: RequestValidationError) -> str:
    parts: list[str] = []
    for error in exc.errors():
        location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
        parts.append(f"{location}: {error.get('msg', 'invalid')}")
    return "; ".join(parts)


def http_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a Starlette/FastAPI ``HTTPException`` as the one error body."""
    error = StudioError(
        code=code_for_status(exc.status_code),
        message=str(exc.detail),
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, exc.status_code)


def unhandled_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    """Log an unexpected failure and return it without internals."""
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    logger.exception("unhandled studio-api error (request_id=%s)", request_id, exc_info=exc)
    error = StudioError(
        code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
        message=f"Something went wrong (request {request_id}). The team has been notified.",
        suggestion="Try again — your work is still safe.",
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, 500)


def _safe_request_id(candidate: str | None) -> str:
    """Return the client's request id when it is safe to echo, else a fresh one."""
    if candidate and REQUEST_ID_PATTERN.match(candidate):
        return candidate
    return uuid4().hex


class RequestIdMiddleware:
    """Accept or mint an ``X-Request-ID`` and echo it on the response."""

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        request_id = _safe_request_id(Headers(scope=scope).get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER))
        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id

        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                MutableHeaders(scope=message)[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = request_id
            await send(message)

        await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)


def register_error_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Install the one-error-body handlers on an app."""
    handler: Any = studio_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(StudioHTTPError, handler)
    handler = validation_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, handler)
    handler = http_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, handler)
    handler = unhandled_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, handler)

and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.

### Without a model

When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:

- A **Working by hand** strip explains the state and offers capture, job map,
  and context.
- Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled
  **Local guidance**.
- Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed;
  outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same
  local repository the model uses.
- Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.

The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.

### The thread is the room

Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront
never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the
customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that
carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for
doing the work.

That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every
artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each
reply with the next move as an action on the surface.

### What it remembers

The studio keeps a small, local, editable model of the person it is helping. It
is not a profile and not a transcript index; it is the handful of things that
change the next answer.

| Kind | What it captures |
|---|---|
| `career` | The PM's role, remit, and what success looks like for them |
| `opportunity` | The opportunity or bet currently in play |
| `business` | Goals, metrics, and commercial constraints |
| `stakeholder` | Who else matters and what they care about |
| `constraint` | Time, budget, policy, or technical limits |
| `evidence` | What has actually been heard or measured |
| `preference` | How the PM likes to work and be spoken to |

Each note is `suggested` or `confirmed`. Suggested notes appear first under
**What I know** with **Yes, that's right**, **That's not it**, and **Edit**;
confirmed notes can be edited or forgotten. The PM can also add a note by hand.
Nothing is silently promoted: the agent may propose, but the person decides.

The agent writes notes through a `remember` tool during a normal reply. The
sidecar applies it, emits a `memory` SSE event, and the panel updates without a
refresh. Memory writes are best-effort — a database failure never turns a good
answer into an error.

The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.

### When the studio is not running

The Living Studio is a local service, and it is the kind of thing that is easy to
forget to start. When the sidecar is not reachable, the SPA does not pretend
otherwise.

- A **subtle strip** across the top of the window says the sidecar isn't running,
  that the assistant is paused and live data is frozen, and offers **Recheck**
  and **Start the sidecar** (opens Settings). It is dismissible for the session
  and clears itself once the sidecar is reached again.
- Sending a message does not fire off a doomed request: it drops a quiet in-thread
  notice pointing to Settings, and the composer never spins.
- The canvas keeps showing the last thing it drew instead of going blank; a failed
  canvas is a failure panel with Retry, not an empty board.

On the CLI, the same condition is `BackendError("could not reach MCP server …")`,
rendered as `Error: …` followed by `Hint: Start the MCP server (python -m
agentic_odi_mcp_server)…`. When the Studio is reached through the free
Cloudflare Worker proxy, a missing `SIDECAR_URL` is reported to the browser as
`{"error": {"code": "mcp_unreachable", "suggestion": "Start the studio sidecar
…"}}` with `X-Request-ID` echoed for support.

### The thread is the room

input.content:
# End-to-end error handling for the Living Studio

2026-10-25 — design for the sidecar/backend-and-error-handling work.

## Goal

A failure anywhere in the stack — the CLI, the sidecar, the hosted Cloudflare
Worker proxy, or the SPA's own network call — should arrive to the user as a
single, human failure: one message, one "what to do", and a clear answer to
"can I retry?". Three non-goals: no stack traces in the UI, no empty screens,
and no dead studio.

## Model

`agentic_odi_core.remote.StudioError` is the one failure shape:
`code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id`. Every layer that
talks to the user maps onto it.

| Layer | Surface |
| --- | --- |
| Core | `message_for_code` / `suggestion_for_code` / `retryable_for_code` (replacing the hard-coded message/detail tables) |
| Sidecar HTTP | `StudioHTTPError(error, status_code)` + handlers in `studio/errors.py`; `router.py` raises it instead of wrapping results in `{"ok": true, "result": …}` |
| Cloudflare Worker | `sidecarError(...)` returns `{"error": StudioError}` and logs unconfigured + unreachable cases; never leaks internals |
| SPA | `asStudioError` classifies server bodies and client-side network failures; `StudioApiError` flows into `FailurePanel` |
| CLI | `BackendError(message, suggestion)` → `Error: …` + `Hint: …` on stderr |

## Status mapping

`STATUS_FOR_CODE` (Python) and `codeForStatus` (TS) map codes ↔ HTTP status:
`mcp_unreachable` → 502, `not_found` → 404, `validation`/`out_of_range` → 422,
`conflict` → 409, `rate_limit` → 429, `internal`/`mcp_tool_failed` → 500.
`MCP_TOOL_FAILED` is intentionally **not retryable** — a model/tool failure
recovers in-turn, not by the user retrying blindly.

## When the sidecar is down

This is the case the work is named for. Two sub-cases:

1. **Hosted (Worker proxy).** The Worker cannot reach `SIDECAR_URL`, or
   `SIDECAR_URL` is unconfigured. `sidecarError` emits `mcp_unreachable` with the
   suggestion "Start the studio sidecar `python scripts/dev.py`…", logs the
   condition, and returns 502. The browser reads `{"error": …}` exactly like any
   other sidecar error — no special casing.

2. **Local (Tauri / dev server).** The browser's `fetch` to `127.0.0.1:8100`
   throws a network `TypeError` before any response arrives. `asStudioError`
   detects this and produces `mcp_unreachable` (not `internal`), so the user
   sees "The studio sidecar isn't reachable" with a start command instead of
   "Something went wrong (request …)".

A `SidecarNotice` strip lives at the top of the window: it only renders once
reachability is confirmed `false` (not while the first probe is in flight), it is
dismissible for the session, and it auto-clears when the next probe succeeds.

## Graceful degradation

- `sendMessage` short-circuits when `sidecarReachable === false`: it drops a
  quiet in-thread notice pointing to Settings instead of starting a doomed
  stream, so the composer never spins on a dead sidecar.
- The canvas keeps showing its last known frame. A failed canvas is a
  `FailurePanel` with Retry, not a blank board — "empty" and "failed" never look
  the same.
- A dropped model only pauses the assistant (`Working by hand` / `OfflineNotice`);
  data writes still go through the local repository.
- The CLI prints `Error: …` then `Hint: …` so a one-liner tells the user what to
  do.

## Request correlation

`RequestIdMiddleware` accepts or mints `X-Request-ID`, echoes it on every
response header and SSE frame, and the unhandled-exception handler includes it
in the message (`Something went wrong (request req-9). The team has been
notified.`) while logging the full traceback server-side. The body never
contains the internal exception text.

## Tests

- `packages/core/tests/test_remote.py`: helper tables and `parse_tool_result`.
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_errors.py` + `test_studio_connectors_router.py`:
  error shape, status mapping, request-id echo. (SPA-build-aware: dynamic-route
  tests disable the SPA fallback so they are hermetic.)
- `tests/test_worker_error_shape.py` / `test_worker_security_headers.py`: Worker
  error body and security headers, source-pinned.
- `apps/studio/src/api/studioApi.test.ts`: `asStudioError` classification +
  `studioError` status mapping.
- `apps/studio/src/components/notices/SidecarNotice.test.tsx`: strip rendering,
  recheck/open/dismiss.
- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.test.tsx`: `sendMessage` short-circuit.
- `apps/cli/tests/test_backend.py`: `BackendError.suggestion`, hint rendering.

"""The build must be deterministic, and the committed output must be current."""

from __future__ import annotations

import build_site
import extract
import pytest
from site_support import DIST, ROOT


def _tree(root):
    return {
        str(path.relative_to(root)): path.read_bytes()
        for path in sorted(root.rglob("*"))
        if path.is_file()
    }


def test_build_is_deterministic(tmp_path):
    first = tmp_path / "a"
    second = tmp_path / "b"
    build_site.build(first)
    build_site.build(second)
    assert _tree(first) == _tree(second)


def test_build_emits_expected_pages(tmp_path):
    build_site.build(tmp_path)
    for rel in ("index.html", "404.html", "sitemap.xml", "robots.txt"):
        assert (tmp_path / rel).is_file()


def test_check_fails_when_output_is_stale(tmp_path):
    build_site.build(tmp_path)
    (tmp_path / "index.html").write_text("stale", encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        build_site.build(tmp_path, check=True)


def test_check_passes_when_output_is_current(tmp_path):
    build_site.build(tmp_path)
    build_site.build(tmp_path, check=True)


def test_the_committed_site_matches_a_fresh_build():
    # The committed output is committed so a reviewer can read the rendered
    # HTML in a pull request. That only works if it is never stale.
    assert DIST.is_dir(), "the site has not been built; run build_site.py"
    build_site.build(DIST, check=True)


def test_the_cli_reference_mentions_every_registered_command():
    # The CLI reference is hand-written, so this is the only thing keeping it
    # from falling behind the commands the CLI actually registers.
    commands = extract.read_cli(ROOT / "apps" / "cli" / "src" / "agentic_odi_cli" / "cli.py")
    reference = (ROOT / "docs" / "cli.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert commands
    missing = [command["name"] for command in commands if command["name"] not in reference]
    assert missing == []

Done. The PR is live at https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/pull/247 with green CI.

## Summary

End-to-end error handling across all four boundaries, unified on the single `StudioError` shape.

**Core** (`packages/core`): replaced hard-coded message/detail tables with `message_for_code` / `suggestion_for_code` / `retryable_for_code`; `MCP_TOOL_FAILED` stays non-retryable (the model recovers in-turn, not the user retrying).

**Sidecar** (`apps/studio-api`): `StudioHTTPError(error, status_code)` + a code↔status map; `router.py` raises it instead of wrapping results in `{"ok": true, ...}`. The unhandled handler includes the request id and never leaks internals; legacy `{"detail": ...}` is still readable.

**Cloudflare Worker** (`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts`): `sidecarError(...)` returns `{"error": StudioError}` (code `mcp_unreachable` for an unreachable/missing `SIDECAR_URL`), logs the conditions on the Worker without leaking internals, and passes `request_id` through. Source-pinned tests in `tests/`.

**SPA** (`apps/studio`):
- `asStudioError` classifies network failures (a thrown `TypeError` when the sidecar is down) as `mcp_unreachable` instead of generic `internal`; `studioError` now maps bare statuses (502→sidecar, 404→not_found, etc.).
- New `SidecarNotice` strip: subtle, persistent, dismissible, recheck + open-Settings actions, auto-clears on reconnect.
- `sendMessage` short-circuits when the sidecar is known down (notice + no doomed stream); the canvas keeps showing its last frame (failed → Retry panel, never blank).
- `FailurePanel` already renders message/detail/suggestion/Retry, so sidecar-returned suggestions flow through to it.

**CLI** (`apps/cli`): `BackendError(message, suggestion)`; `run_tool` prints `Error: …` then `Hint: …`, and the MCP transport layer attaches a start-server hint to unreachable/timeout failures.

Docs updated (`docs/architecture/data-flow.md`, `docs/living-studio.md`) plus a design note at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-error-handling-design-design.md`; README was already accurate on the referenced commands.

**Verification (all green on the committed tree):** pytest 1001 passed · vitest 259 passed · mypy · ruff check · ruff format --check · bandit · render check · tsc · eslint · build · gen:api-types (no drift) · website build.

One thing worth flagging: my earlier `npm run build` created `apps/studio/dist`, which mounts the SPA catch-all route and shadows dynamically-added `/api/*` routes in three `test_studio_errors.py` tests — I made those hermetic (disabled the SPA fallback) rather than leave them coupled to build artifacts.

 # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
 
 This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
 
 > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
 
 ---
 
 ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
 
 This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
 
 ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
 
 ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
 
 ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
 
 - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
 - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
 - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
 - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
 
 - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
 - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
 - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
 
   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
 
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
 
 - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
 
 - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
 - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
 
 - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
 
 - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
 
   ```
   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
   ```
 
 - **Interpretation**:
   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
 
 - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
 - Segments can be:
   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
 
 Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
 
 | Strategy | When to use |
 |---|---|
 | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
 | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
 | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
 
 ---
 
 ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
 
 These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
 
 | DO | DON'T |
 |---|---|
 | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
 | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
 | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
 | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
 | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
 | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
 | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |
 
 ---
 
 ## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
 - **Language**: Python 3.10+
 - **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
 - **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
 - **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
 - **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
 - **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
 - **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
 - **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`
 
 ---
 
 ## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail
 
 `README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
 high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
 in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
 times.
 
 ### When to update
 
 Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:
 
 | Change type | Where to update |
 |---|---|
 | New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
 | New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
 | New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
 | New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
 | New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
 | New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
 | New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
+| New message part or conversation capability | `docs/living-studio.md` (conversation runtime) |
 | Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
 | Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
 | Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |
 
 ### Rules
 
 - ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
 - ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
 - ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
 - ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
 - ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
 - ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.
 
 ---
 
 ## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails
 
 ### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
 - **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
 - **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
   - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
   - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
 - **Tool Creation**: 
   - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
   - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
   - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.
 
 ### 2. Async / Client Practices
 - Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
 - Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.
 
 ### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
 - Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
 - When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.
 
 ### 4. General Philosophy
 - **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
 - **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
 - **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
 - **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.
 
-### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
+### 5. Conversation UI (assistant-ui)
+
+The Studio's transcript is [assistant-ui](https://www.assistant-ui.com) bound to
+our own store; it is not a hand-rolled message list. Do not replace it, wrap it in
+a second one, or re-implement streaming, the composer, attachments, branches, or
+approval prompts beside it.
+
+- **One bridge.** `apps/studio/src/assistant/convert.ts` is the only mapping
+  between `ChatMessage`/`ChatPart` and assistant-ui parts. It is pure and tested
+  without a runtime. A new part type is added there, rendered in `parts.tsx`, and
+  registered in the `components` map in `Conversation.tsx` — three files, never a
+  fourth path.
+- **The store stays ours.** `state/StudioContext.tsx` owns messages, ids,
+  `parentId`, streaming state, memory, and canvas invalidation. The runtime is
+  presentation: `useExternalStoreRuntime` in `assistant/StudioRuntime.tsx` maps
+  `onNew`, `onEdit`, `onReload`, `onCancel`, `setMessages`, and
+  `onRespondToToolApproval` onto context actions. Do not let component state
+  become a second source of truth.
+- **The SSE contract stays additive.** The sidecar is a Python tool loop; it is
+  not migrating to Vercel's AI SDK stream protocol. New capability arrives as a
+  new event (`reasoning`, `source`, `approval`, `ui`, …) or a new opt-in request
+  field, and a client that sends neither must see the old stream unchanged.
+- **The ODI catalog stays ours.** Generated surfaces travel as assistant-ui

+- **No fabricated provenance.** A source names what a turn actually read; a part

+- **Approvals gate writes, not reads.** `approvals: true` pauses mutating tools
